# A board family: columns, swimlanes and cards on one store

## Context

Leaf of #20874. It adds the first of four families: a kanban board. It depends on none of the others.

## The Problem

The engine has no board. An app that tracks work in columns builds one from lists and drag zones by hand, and the result owns its data, so a second window or an agent cannot follow a move.

## The Architectural Reality

- Sibling families: `src/grid` and `src/calendar`. Where a module lands inside `src/board` (for example a `model` or `store` subfolder as in `src/calendar`) is decided by the structural pre-flight in the pull request.
- Data: one `data.Store` of card records; a column is a predicate over a field of those records, never a list of its own.
- Drag: reuse the `Neo.draggable` sort zones and the per-window drag coordinator on the main thread (`Neo.main.addon.DragDrop`). It keeps one registration per drag root and one active zone per gesture, so the card zone and the column zone register side by side and keep distinct identities.
- Styles: `resources/scss/src/board` plus one folder per theme. The engine ships five themes; this leaf brings `theme-neo-dark` and `theme-neo-light`, and the other three are a leaf of their own.
- Guards the pull request meets: the file-size guard (`buildScripts/util/check-file-sizes.mjs`, 1,000 code lines), the ticket-archaeology check (no ticket numbers in source comments), the class-module-scope lint, and JSDoc with `@summary` on every class and method.

## The Fix

Add the family under `Neo.board`: a container, a column and its body, a lane row for swimlanes, a card with its items, a card model, a card editor, a selection model for cards, and two sort zones (cards and columns). The implementation exists and lands in one pull request with its unit specs, its styles for the two neo themes and one example, `examples/board/basic`, listed in the examples index.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behaviour | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.board.*` (new) | this ticket | columns project one store; a move is one record change; swimlanes, editor, keyboard and ARIA, multi-card drag, column reordering, a per-column count with an optional limit | none: the family is new | JSDoc; the guide is a later leaf | the family's unit specs and the example |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The classes exist under `Neo.board` and appear in the output of `npm run generate-docs-json`.
- [ ] The family's unit specs pass in the engine's unit configuration.
- [ ] `examples/board/basic` runs in the four environments, is listed in the examples index, and a card moved there is a single record change that a second view on the same store shows.
- [ ] The board is styled in `theme-neo-dark` and `theme-neo-light`.
- [ ] **Look:** the pull request carries a frame of `examples/board/basic` in each of the two themes, and the epic's design read (#20874) passes on them: no control in the example's own chrome is left in its default style, and every affordance of the family (cards, drop targets, drag proxies, column headers) reads as designed in both themes.
- [ ] The file-size, ticket-archaeology and lint guards pass.

## Out of Scope

The three other themes and the guide (their own leaves). Server-backed columns. A drag across windows.

- 2026-11-17T04:04:34Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `2d1c2ed` - "fix(board): repair record adoption, column drags, lanes, saves, ids and stores (#20875)

A lazy store's rows become their canonical Records before a card or a writer captures them, and getSourceRecord hydrates a hidden row.

Column drags admit on columnsResortable alone: the base SortZone reads its owner switch through isResortable(), which ColumnSortZone overrides.

A record change that brings a new status and a new lane projects the new column into every lane.

A Save against a Record that a reload or a replacement store retired writes nothing; the editor rebinds to the current Record of the same key, or hides when the key is gone.

Board.slug keeps types apart, so the number key 1 and the string key '1' get distinct ids.

The board retires the stores it creates, on replacement and on destroy, never a store it was handed."
